articles.title: French blood banks hacked in latest cyber-attack on Europe
articles.summary:
Temperature and defrosting thresholds raised to ‘very high levels’ at three cold stores stocking vital blood products

  • Europe live – latest updates

France’s national blood service has said hackers accessed control systems and boosted temperatures at three cold stores stocking vital blood products, in an apparent escalation of recent cyber-attacks on fridges and freezers across Europe.

The French blood service (EFS) said temperature and defrosting thresholds had been raised to “very high levels” in the attack, adding that its alarm systems had allowed technicians to intervene before the products were compromised.

articles.title: ‘The point was to dehumanise’: London Holocaust archive examines world’s first ‘viral’ antisemitism scandal
articles.summary:
Dreyfus affair has echoes of how anti-Jewish hatred manifests itself today, say curators at Weiner Library

It was the world’s first experience of antisemitism “gone viral”, said Barbara Warnock, a co-director of the oldest Holocaust archive, the Wiener Holocaust Library in London.

It was 1894 and printing presses were faster than ever before. France’s prohibitive censorship laws had been lifted, and then along came the Dreyfus affair: a public shouting match that followed the wrongful conviction for treason of Alfred Dreyfus, a 36-year-old French army captain.

articles.title: ‘We are a threat to Putin’: the small Norwegian news outlet with half its staff on Russia’s wanted list
articles.summary:
Exiled journalists at the Barents Observer face growing intimidation as Moscow seeks to control media beyond its borders

The official newspaper of the Russian government is an unlikely source of recognition for a European news outlet critical of Vladimir Putin and providing sanctuary to exiled Russian journalists. But in May, two days after Russia tested its new intercontinental ballistic missile system nicknamed “Satan II” by Nato, an article in Rossiyskaya Gazeta prompted celebrations in a remote newsroom in the Arctic.

The story about how “leading global media” reacted to the Sarmat missile test referred to just a handful of outlets including the BBC, Reuters, the Associated Press and France 24. But among them was the Barents Observer, a small, journalist-owned online newspaper publishing in English and Russian about northern Russia and the Euro-Arctic region from a modest office in the north-eastern Norwegian town of Kirkenes.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí hlubokému smutku a politickým otřesům po tragické srážce vysokorychlostních vlaků ve Španělsku, která si vyžádala 68 obětí. Simultaneously, key EU-Canada summits are advancing energy and defense cooperation, while a local truce holds in Ukraine and Serbia's authoritarian regime collapses under student-led pressure.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí kombinaci politické nestability po neočekávaném odchodu šéfky ECB Christine Lagardeové a křehkému ekonomickému růstu, který v klíčových zemích jako Francie flirtuje s recesí.
